questions.q:
The correct statements regarding froth floatation method in metallurgy are
I. Used for the purification of sulphide ores
II. Used for the roasting of sulphide ores
III. It is based on the relative densities of gangue and ore particles
IV. It is based on the difference in the wetting properties of gangue and ore particles in frothing agent and water
questions.solution: The froth floatation process is used for the concentration (purification) of ores, specially sulphide ores. It is based on the principle of relative preference of wetting of gangue and ore particles in water and frothing agent. Thus, I and IV are correct.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is not correct?
(i) Froth-floatation is used for removing gangue from sulphide ore.
(ii) Cresols are used to stabilise the froth.
(iii) Sodium cyanide can be used as depressant for preferential separation.
(iv) Aniline can be used as froth enhancer.
questions.solution: Froth-flotation is a process for selectively separating hydrophobic materials from hydrophilic. This is used in mineral processing, paper recycling and waste water. Aniline or cresols are added to stabilise the froth, not for froth enhancer. Hence, the correct option is (4).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q:
Match the following items of List-I with those of List-II \(
List IList II
(A)Nickel(1)Electrolytic refining
(B)Titanium(2)Zone refining
(C)Germanium(3)van-Arkel method
(D)Copper(4)Mond process
\) The correct answer is
questions.solution:
(A) The Mond process, sometimes known as the carbonyl process, is a technique created by Ludwig Mond in 1890, to extract and purify nickel. Thus, correct match for (A) - (4).
(B) van Arkel method is used for refining zirconium or titanium. In this method, oxygen and nitrogen, present as impurity are removed by heating metal in an evacuated vessel with iodine. Thus, correct match for (B) - (3).
(C) Zone refining is a very useful method to get metals with very high purity such as silicon and germanium. Thus, correct match for (c)-(2).
(D) Many metals, such as copper, zinc, tin, nickel, silver, gold etc. are refined by electrolysis. In this process, the impure metal is made the anode and a thin strip of pure metal is made the cathode. The solution of the metal salt is used as an electrolyte. Thus, correct match for (D) - (1).
Hence, the correct option is (c).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: In the extraction of silver, zinc metal is used as a reducing agent. What is the molecular structure of the zinc complex formed in this reaction?
questions.solution:
During extraction of silver, the finely powdered silver ore is treated with dilute KCN solution to form a cyano complex of silver. This complex is water soluble.
\(\mathrm{Ag}_{2} \mathrm{ S}+4 \mathrm{NaCN} \rightleftharpoons2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+ \mathrm{Na}}_{2} \mathrm{ S}\)
Then zinc is added to the solution. More electropositive zinc displaces silver from the complex.
\(\left.2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+ \mathrm{Zn} \longrightarrow \mmathrm{Na}}_{2} \left[\mmathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right)+2 \mathrm{Ag}\right]\)
In $\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{CN})_2$, zinc adopts the tetrahedral coordination environment, all linked by bridging cyanide ligands.
Hence, the correct option is (a).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q:
Which statement is incorrect regarding Hall-Heroult process for metallurgy of aluminium?
1. Use of \($\mathrm{Na}}_{3}  \mathrm{AlF}$}_{6}\) lowers the melting point of \($\mathrm{Al}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}$}_{3}\)
2. Steel vessel with lining of carbon acts as cathode.
3. Graphite is used as anode.
4. Carbon dioxide gas is generated at cathode.
questions.solution:
In Hall-Heroult process for extraction of aluminium (crude) from alumina \($\left(\mathrm{Al}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}$}_{3}\right)\).
Statements (1), (2) and (3) are correct because cryolite \($\left(\mathrm{Na}}_{3}  \mathrm{AlF}$}_{6}\right)\) is added to \($\mathrm{Al}}_{2}  \mathrm{O}$}_{3}\) to lower, its melting point. Here, steel vessel with lining of carbon acts as cathode and graphite acts as anode, but statement (4) is incorrect because \($\mathrm{Al}$\) gets deposited at cathode.

questions.q: Calamine, bauxite, malachite and siderite respectively are ores of.........
questions.solution:
Calamine \(\mathrm{ZnCO}}_{3}\) is the ore of \(\mathrm{Zn}$\). Bauxite, \( \mathrm{AlO}_x( \mathrm{OH})_{3-2 x}\) is the ore of \(\mathrm{Al}\). (where, \(0  <  x <  1\))
Malachite, \(\mathrm{CuCO}$}_{3} $\cdot \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{OH})_$2\) is the ore of \(\mathrm{Cu}$\). Siderite, \(\mathrm{FeCO}}_{3}\) is the ore of \(\mathrm{Fe}$\).

questions.q:
Identify the correct statements from the following:
i. In the extraction of \($\mathrm{Ag}$\) and \($\mathrm{Au}$\), zinc is used as reducing agent.
ii. Impure zinc can be refined by distillation method.
iii. Malachite is an ore of nickel.
questions.solution:
The explanations of given statements are as follows:
(i) In the extraction of $\mathrm{Ag}$ and $\mathrm{Au}$, zinc is used as reducing agent.
\($\begin{array}{r}
2\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right](a q)+\mathrm{Zn}(s) \longrightarrow 2 \mmathrm{Ag}(s)+{\left[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}(a q)}
\end{array}$
Thus, statement (i) is correct.
(ii) Impure zinc can be refined by the process of distillation.
Thus, statement (ii) is correct.
(iii) Malachite, $(\left[\m$mathrm{Cu}_2\left(\mathrm{CO}_{3}\$\right)(\mathrm{OH})_2\right]\) is an ore of copper. Thus, statement (iii) is incorrect. Hence, correct option is (d).

\(\mathrm{I}$}_{2}\) is used for refining Ti metal using van Arkel method. questions.q: The pair of metals refined by "vapour phase refining" is
questions.solution:
Vapour phase refining process involves conversion& of a metal& into a volatile compound and then it is decomposed to obtain pure metal.

Nickel& is purified by Mond& process: Impure nickel& is heated in a stream& of carbon monoxide to form a volatile complex which is further decomposed to obtain pure nickel.

$Ni + 4CO\overset{350K}{→}Ni\left(CO\right)^{4}\overset{470K}{→}Ni ( pure ) + 4CO$

Van Arkel method: Zirconium or titanium is purified by this method. Zirconium is heated in iodine vapours to form a volatile complex at $870K$ which is further decomposed to obtain pure metal.

$Zr + 2{I}_{2}\overset{870K}{→}{ZrI}_{4}\overset{1800K}{→}Zr ( pure ) + 2{I}_{2}$&

questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: The ore which is concentrated by leaching
questions.solution:
Leaching is a process in which powdered ore is treated with certain reagents, which dissolves the ore leaving behind impurities in undissolved form. Aluminium ore is concentrated by this method, bauxite $\left(\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)$ contain ferric oxide, titanium oxide and silica as impurities.
Bauxite is treated with aqueous solution of caustic soda. Alumina get dissolved forming soluble sodium aluminate leaving behind impurities.

questions.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
questions.q: What is the role of limestone during the extraction of iron from haematite ore?
questions.solution: During extraction of iron from haematite ore, roasted ore, along with coke and limestone is heated in blast furnance. Here coke behaves as reducing agent and limestone is worked as flux. In this process, in reducing zone $\left(400-900^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\right)$, spongy iron is obtained. In slag zone $\left(900-1200^{{}^{\circ}}\right)$, limestone reacts with impurity (e.g., silica) to form slag. In the combustion and fusion zone $\left(1200-1600^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}\right)$, all the charge melts and pig iron is obtained which purified further.

questions.q: Which of the following is not added during the extraction of silver by cyanide process?
questions.solution:
In the extraction of silver from cyanide process (also Mac-Arthur Forrest process), the siliver compound dissolve in $\mathrm{NaCN}$ solution forming a
soluble complex salt, in presence of air, then silver is precipitated from this complex salt by the addition of $\mathrm{Zn}$, because $\mathrm{Zn}$ being more reactive displaces the Ag.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Ag}_2 \mathrm{ S}+4 \mathrm{NaCN} & \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ S} \downarrow \\ \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{ S}+2 \mathrm{O}_2 & \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4 \\ 2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{CN})_2\right]+\mathrm{Zn} & \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_2\left[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]+2 \mathrm{Ag} \downarrow\end{aligned}$

questions.q: During the electrolysis of cryolite, aluminium and fluorine are formed in........ molar ratio :
questions.solution:
Electrolysis of cryolite can be explained as
$\mathrm{Na}_3 \mathrm{AlF}_6 \rightleftharpoons 3 \mathrm{NaF}+\mathrm{AlF}_34 \mathrm{AlF}_3 \rightleftharpoons 4 \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+12 \mathrm{ F}^{-}\begin{array}{cc}+12 e^{-} \downarrow & \downarrow-12 e^{-} \\ 4 \mathrm{Al} & 6 \mathrm{ F}_2\end{array}$
(At cathode) (At anode)
So, the molar ratio of $\mathrm{Al}$ and $\mathrm{F}_2$ is $4: 6=2: 3$.
